clue.text: Hopin' for relief when achin'

definitions.meaning: hoping, with the final g dropped as in the clue, is aspiring
a common painkiller taken to ease aches

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for something to ease their pain, written in a casual dropped-g style.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g's are the trick: 'Hopin'' stands for aspirin', the clipped form of aspiring, which matches the painkiller letter for letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The painkiller is a standard remedy for aches, and aspiring means hoping, here clipped like the clue's words.

clue.text: Humiliated by a spurious education

parts.note: something spurious is fake, a sham

explanation.surface: Someone feels belittled because their schooling turned out to be fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ashamed is the synonym: a humiliated person is shamed and embarrassed.

clue.text: Patrol leader takes girl in with force — if force makes a controller of development

parts.note: PL is the Scouts' abbreviation for a patrol leader
Ann is a girl's name
taken as written
g stands for gravitational force, as in g-force

indicators.note: makes is read as 'is made into', so the letters of the words before it get rearranged

explanation.surface: A scout leader brings a girl along and uses force to control things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges IF FORCE into OFFICER. The first 'force' gives only G, the second is anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: A local-council official who decides on building permission controls development in an area.

clue.text: Rubbish and untidy mess — nature of an all-rounder?

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the word untidy is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone complains about rubbish and a messy room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' is the anagram signal on the word beside it; 'all-rounder' is cricket slang for a player who bats and bowls, here read as a round person.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundness or plumpness is the quality of being round all over, playfully called the nature of an all-rounder.

clue.text: She's not quite like other girls

definitions.note: the definition is she; the 's is is, a link

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: being like everybody else is being normal

explanation.surface: A girl is a bit different from her friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the final L from NORMAL. NORMA is a girl's name, so 'She' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name such as this one fits a clue word meaning a particular female person.

clue.text: Shield to absorb impact?

definitions.meaning: a small round shield held in the hand
something that buckles crumples under a blow, taking the impact

explanation.surface: A shield designed to soak up blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round hand shield bears this name, and one that buckles crumples, soaking up a blow.

clue.text: Señor of the road as well as in the dance

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: the bolero is a Spanish dance
as well as means and

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman is found both on the road and on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. A bandolero is a Spanish highwayman, hence 'Señor of the road'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish bandit or highwayman, a gentleman robber of the roads, is called this.

clue.text: Bird with covered head

definitions.meaning: a castrated cockerel fattened for the table
wearing a hat is having your ...

explanation.surface: A bird whose head is covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated rooster is a kind of bird, and wearing a hat means having a cap on.

clue.text: What to do if the puzzle is too difficult

definitions.text: What to do if the puzzle is too difficult

parts.words: What to do if the puzzle is too difficult
parts.note: the advice for a crossword you cannot finish is simply to abandon it partly done

explanation.surface: Advice to a solver who is stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning a task part-done is exactly what you do with a crossword beyond you.

clue.text: Staff guarding art collection took turns

indicators.note: one piece guarding another stands round it, so it holds it inside

parts.note: a staff is a rod
the Tate is the national art gallery in London

explanation.surface: Gallery staff keep watch over the artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' is the container signal; the Tate is a famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rotated a duty is to have taken turns at it, or simply to have spun round.

clue.text: Operation of falling in love?

parts.note: when you fall in love you give your heart to someone else, a kind of surgical transfer

explanation.surface: A question about what happens when people fall in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical procedure moving the blood-pumping organ to a new body; lovers figuratively give theirs away.

clue.text: Gate for those facing the bowling

definitions.meaning: the war memorial gate at Ypres in Belgium
in cricket the batsmen at the crease are the ...

explanation.surface: An entrance meant for the batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side's players at the wicket are 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Menin Gate is the Ypres war memorial, and the batters at the wicket are the men in.

clue.text: Mend a torn dress with decoration

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or prepare, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Repair a ripped frock and add some trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a garment; it is the verb rearranging MEND A TORN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament or embellishment is a decoration, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: In Scotland they say 'Thicko! Stupid!'

indicators.note: they say signals that we hear the words spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a thicko is a dunce, and stupid is inane

explanation.surface: Scots trade insults about someone's intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' turns DUNCE INANE into a sound-alike of the Scottish hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunsinane is the hill in Perthshire famous from Macbeth, so it is a place in Scotland.

clue.text: European Union bearing modified vegetable produce

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brussels rules on genetically modified vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges EU plus BEARING.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine, called eggplant in America, is a purple vegetable crop.

clue.text: Journalist, having gone to jail, is given corporal punishment

indicators.note: the journalist going to the jail means ED comes after CAN

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is jailed and beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having gone to' sets the order: the journalist follows the jail. 'Can' is American and British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caned is to be beaten with a stick, a form of corporal punishment.

clue.text: Once worn, often battered

definitions.meaning: a pouch worn over the crotch by men in former times
portions of cod fish are usually fried in batter

explanation.surface: Something worn once and frequently beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' suggests beaten, but means coated in batter, as fish is in British fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor pouch is a historical garment, and portions of cod are commonly fried in batter.

clue.text: BT swapped wooden spoon for other prize

indicators.note: B and T swapped means one B gives way to a T

parts.note: the wooden spoon is a booby prize, given to whoever comes last

explanation.surface: A telecoms firm trades a joke award for a better one.
explanation.walkthrough: BT looks like the phone company but is just B swapped for T. A wooden spoon is the joke prize for coming last in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot or plunder is a prize of another kind, taken rather than awarded.

clue.text: Country girl from Birmingham, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: Olivia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A country lass comes from Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country girl' wants to be read as one idea; 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a landlocked South American nation.

clue.text: To Nelson it meant a load of balls

definitions.text: To Nelson it meant a load of balls

parts.words: To Nelson it meant a load of balls
parts.note: in Nelson's navy, firing every cannon on one side of a ship at once sent a mass of cannonballs

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson apparently thought something was nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a load of balls' is British slang for nonsense; read literally it is a volley of cannonballs.
explanation.definitionFit: A simultaneous firing of all guns on one side of a warship, delivering many cannonballs.

clue.text: Arithmetic is rejected by renaissance scholar

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: arithmetic is sums
with plural sums, is becomes are

explanation.surface: A scholar of the Renaissance dismisses arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the reversal signal; 'is' must become plural to agree with sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the leading Dutch humanist of the Renaissance.

clue.text: What nurses did after a shift, turning to port

definitions.text: What nurses did after a shift
definitions.meaning: at the end of a shift nurses left the hospital wards
port is the left side of a ship, so turning that way

explanation.surface: Nurses finish work and head off.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the nautical term for the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Going towards the left, since port is the left side of a ship, and nurses leaving their wards.

clue.text: Former SM first to wind round

indicators.note: first puts the warrant officer before the other piece

parts.note: a sergeant major is a warrant officer, WO
former means old

explanation.surface: An ex-sergeant major goes first to wind something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' fixes the order. A sergeant major holds a warrant officer's rank in the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical verb for binding a rope tightly round a spar, so to wind round it.

clue.text: Robes embroidered, but not gaudy

indicators.note: embroidered means elaborated or worked over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Decorated gowns that are nonetheless tasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidered' rearranges ROBES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober colours are subdued and plain, the opposite of gaudy.

clue.text: One with a concern in a holiday resort

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a concern is a business, biz for short

explanation.surface: Someone with a business in a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts BIZ inside I A; the second 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Balearic island famed as a Mediterranean party destination.

clue.text: Posh station with a junction wanting space down the line

parts.note: Victoria is a London railway terminus

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the space is removed

parts.note: Beckenham Junction is a station in south London
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A smart London station has a junction further along the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' drops EN from BECKENHAM. Beckenham Junction lies down the line from Victoria; 'Posh' was her Spice Girls nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer was known as Posh Spice in the Spice Girls, so the nickname defines her.

clue.text: Contract given to a composer

parts.note: Frank Bridge was an English composer

explanation.surface: A composer is handed a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun; it is the verb meaning shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text is to contract or condense it.

clue.text: Lives with corrupt desires

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Living with depraved urges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges DESIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives somewhere dwells there, a straight synonym.
